h: Antler Season, Lavender Fields and Wader Tides
p: Red deer change dramatically through the year, which means a deer safari at Snettisham Park can feel different every time you go. In spring, stags shed their antlers and start growing new ones covered in soft velvet. By late summer the antlers have hardened, and in autumn comes the rut, when stags roar, strut and square up to one another to win the attention of the hinds. Ask the kids to guess which season it is from the antlers alone and see who gets it right.

Being a working farm attraction, seasonal events and activities shift through the year, so look up what's on before you go and you might catch something extra special. Bring hand gel for after the animal handling, a spare set of clothes for the youngest, and a waterproof for the safari trailer. A picnic is a nice touch on a dry day too.

Snettisham's coast is home to an RSPB reserve on the shores of the Wash, where on the very biggest high tides tens of thousands of wading birds are pushed off the mudflats and swirl overhead in huge, shimmering flocks. Birders call it the wader spectacular, and it's worth planning around a tide table if you're keen. Just up the road at Heacham, Norfolk Lavender grows its fragrant purple fields, at their prettiest in high summer. And the Sandringham estate, the King's Norfolk retreat, has a big country park with woodland walks and play areas that are open to wander. That's three very different moods within a few miles of each other.
